extracted.intended_audience: ORR staff, care provider facilities, legal service providers, sponsors, and public commenters on the NPRM
extracted.subtask_description: Extracted standards and requirements from ORR's proposed rule (NPRM) governing care, transportation, transfers, data/reporting, age determinations, disability accommodations, medication administration, emergency/influx operations, and legal services for unaccompanied children.

rubrics_metrics.name: ORR funding and promotion of pro bono and legal services
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR may expand access to pro bono services and fund legal services in immigration-related proceedings or matters and may promote pro bono services and fund legal services for broader purposes related to protecting unaccompanied children from mistreatment, exploitation, and trafficking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ORR provides each child with lists of pro bono providers by state and national organizations upon admission; ORR-funded providers may help coordinate referrals. ORR recognizes it may be impracticable to secure pro bono services when demand exceeds supply and proposes discretion to fund legal services for specific purposes based on judgment and priorities; may make grants or contracts, including for children released from ORR care (formula or geographic distribution), subject to available resources and appropriations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumption against retaliation for legal service providers
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR shall presume that legal service providers are acting in good faith and shall not retaliate against a legal service provider for actions taken within the scope of their responsibilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: ORR shall not engage in retaliatory actions against providers or representatives for reporting harm or misconduct on behalf of a child. ORR retains responsibility to manage the UC program (considering child interests, placement policies, infrastructure, and personnel).

rubrics_metrics.name: Informed consent and oversight for psychotropic medications
rubrics_metrics.description: Except in the case of a psychiatric emergency, ORR must ensure that, whenever possible, authorized individuals provide informed consent prior to administration of psychotropic medications to unaccompanied children.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ORR would ensure meaningful oversight of psychotropic medication administration, e.g., review of cases flagged by care providers and secondary retrospective reviews based on factors such as child's age, number of medications prescribed, or dosages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of Section 504 protections and complaint procedures for children with disabilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide notice of protections against discrimination assured by section 504 (45 CFR part 85) and the available procedures for seeking reasonable modifications or making a complaint about alleged discrimination while in ORR custody.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ORR proposes to codify notice requirements so children are informed of protections and procedures; ties to ongoing litigation are noted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Most integrated setting requirement for children with disabilities
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR shall administer the UC Program in the most integrated setting appropriate to the needs of qualified unaccompanied children with disabilities, in accordance with 45 CFR 85.21(d), unless ORR can demonstrate a fundamental alteration would occur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 'most integrated setting' enables interaction with non-disabled individuals to the fullest extent possible; ORR may demonstrate fundamental alteration to avoid compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable modifications for children with disabilities; documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR would provide reasonable modifications to the UC Program for each child with one or more disabilities as needed to ensure equal access, but is not required to take actions that would result in a fundamental alteration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Services, supports, and program modifications provided must be documented in the child's case file where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Release assessments must consider child's disability and enable reasonable modifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of a potential sponsor's capability to provide for the child's physical and mental well-being must include explicit consideration of the impact of the child's disability(ies).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PRS (post-release services) must make reasonable modifications in policies/practices/procedures to enable released children with disabilities to live in the most integrated setting; ORR will affirmatively support sponsors in accessing community-based services; ORR will not delay release solely because post-release services are not in place.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transportation appropriate to child's age and needs
rubrics_metrics.description: Care provider facilities must transport a child in a manner appropriate to the child's age and physical and mental needs, including proper use of car seats for young children, consistent with proposed §410.1304.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Individuals transporting children may use de-escalation or positive behavior management techniques to ensure safety, as explained in §410.1304(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on use of soft restraints during transport
rubrics_metrics.description: Care provider facilities may only use soft restraints (e.g., zip ties and leg or ankle weights) during transport to and from secure facilities, and only when the facility believes the child poses a serious risk of physical harm to self or others or a serious risk of running away.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Secure facilities, except for RTCs, may restrain a child for immediate safety during transport to immigration court or an asylum interview as discussed in §410.1304(e)(2) and (f).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely assistance with transportation for release to sponsors
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR would assist without undue delay in making transportation arrangements where it has approved the release of a child to a sponsor and may require the care provider to transport the child.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ORR may reimburse the care provider facility or pay directly for the child and/or sponsor's transportation as appropriate to facilitate timely release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with state and local licensing and transportation regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: Care provider facilities shall comply with all relevant State and local licensing requirements and state and Federal regulations regarding transportation of children, such as meeting/exceeding minimum staff/child ratios and maintaining/inspecting vehicles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If state law conflicts with ORR regulations or an ORR employee's federal duties, the ORR employee must abide by federal duties; ORR will review conflicts to ensure statutory responsibilities are met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Background checks for drivers transporting children
rubrics_metrics.description: Care provider facilities must conduct all necessary background checks for drivers transporting unaccompanied children, in compliance with proposed §410.1305(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Codifies existing policy as a regulatory requirement to ensure driver suitability and child safety during transport.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transport staffing: same-gender staff presence when possible
rubrics_metrics.description: If a care provider facility is transporting a child, at least one transport staff of the same gender as the child being transported must be present in the vehicle to the greatest extent possible under the circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Codifies existing ORR policy to safeguard child dignity and safety during transport.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data collection and periodic reporting of specified child information
rubrics_metrics.description: Care provider facilities are required to maintain and periodically report to ORR data including biographical information, date entered Federal custody, documentation of placement, transfer, removal, release, detention rationale, and disposition of actions in which the child is the subject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed §410.1501(a)-(e) enumerates required fields; reporting enables ORR to compile statistical information and meet HSA obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting of assessments and evaluation data to improve care
rubrics_metrics.description: Care provider facilities must document and periodically report information gathered from assessments, evaluations, or reports of the child and other data necessary to evaluate and improve care and services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ORR proposes inclusion of additional fields (e.g., indigenous origin) not specifically enumerated in statute because they support program duties; see §410.1501(f)-(g).

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuous assessment and least restrictive placement standard for transfers
rubrics_metrics.description: Care provider facilities must continuously assess a child to ensure placements are appropriate and place children in the least restrictive setting that is in their best interests, subject to danger-to-self/community and runaway risk considerations (TVPRA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Care providers must follow ORR policy guidance regarding placement considerations when recommending transfers and ensure health and safety in placement decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for transfer recommendations and medical clearance timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: Care provider facilities must make transfer recommendations if an alternate placement better meets a child's needs; when ORR transfers a child, the current facility must ensure the child is medically cleared for transfer within three business days, unless waived by ORR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For acute/chronic medical conditions or those requiring heightened ORR involvement, staff and ORR must meet to review transfer recommendations. If not medically cleared within three business days, notify ORR; ORR makes final determination on fitness for travel and will specify timeframe for re-evaluation if denied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transfer notification timeframes to interested parties
rubrics_metrics.description: Referring care provider must notify all appropriate interested parties (child, child's attorney of record, legal service provider, Child Advocate, and potentially EOIR) within 48 hours prior to physical transfer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advanced notice not required in unusual and compelling circumstances, but notice must be provided within 24 hours following the transfer in such cases. ORR believes the 48-hour rule provides effective timeline while allowing necessary flexibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for transfer of possessions, legal papers, and medications
rubrics_metrics.description: Children must be transferred with their possessions and legal papers; possessions exceeding carrier limits must be shipped timely. Children must be transferred with a 30-day supply of medications where applicable, and the accepting provider must be instructed in proper medication administration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Codifies paragraph 27 of the FSA and existing practice to preserve continuity of care and legal access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Periodic review of restrictive placements every 30 days and documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: When children are placed in restrictive settings (secure, heightened supervision, or RTC), the receiving facility and ORR must review placement at least every 30 days to determine if a different level of care is appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If continued restrictive placement is necessary, the care provider must document and, upon request, provide the rationale for continued placement to the child's attorney of record, legal service provider, and Child Advocate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Group transfer requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: When transferring more than one child at a time (group transfers), care provider facilities must follow ORR policy guidance and the substantive requirements in §410.1601(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Group transfers typically occur due to emergencies or program closures; clarifying requirements helps ensure safety and health of multiple children in transfer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporary transfers during emergency situations and notification timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: In emergencies, care provider facilities may temporarily change a child's physical placement prior to securing ORR permission, but must notify ORR as soon as possible and in all cases within eight hours of transfer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consistent with HSA and TVPRA, child remains in ORR legal custody and may only be transferred or released by ORR; notification allows ORR oversight while permitting necessary emergency actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preference to minimize transfers to promote stability
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR expresses a preference to minimize the transfer of a child and limit transfers to situations necessary to promote stability and encourage relationship establishment, particularly among vulnerable children.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ORR solicits public comment on provisions related to minimizing transfers and placements for children with disabilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Age determination: trigger and general standard
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR will only conduct age determination procedures if there is reasonable suspicion the individual is not a minor, and procedures must consider the totality of circumstances and evidence rather than rely on any single piece of evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This approach balances concerns for true unaccompanied children and accurate age identification; proposed §410.1309 requires notice to legal counsel regarding age determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible evidence for age determinations (non-exclusive list)
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR may consider multiple forms of evidence including birth certificates (original, certified copy, photocopy; may consult consulate), authentic government-issued documents, baptismal/school/medical records, sworn affidavits from relatives, statements by the individual, statements from parents or others, and medical age assessments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Medical age assessments should not be used as the sole determining factor but only in concert with other evidence; proposed §410.1703 enumerates these options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medical age assessment probability threshold and treatment of ambiguous results
rubrics_metrics.description: When used with other evidence, a medical age assessment indicating a 75 percent or greater probability that the individual is 18 or older may be accepted as one piece of evidence in favor of an adult finding; ambiguous or borderline forensic results are resolved in favor of finding the individual is a minor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examining doctor must submit a written report indicating the probability percentage. ORR will not rely solely on medical assessments; totality of evidence is required to determine age.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of individual determined to be adult by totality of evidence and re-evaluation rights
rubrics_metrics.description: If totality of evidence leads a reasonable person to conclude an individual is an adult despite claiming to be under 18, ORR will treat the person as an adult for all purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The individual or their attorney may present new information at any time for re-evaluation. If re-evaluation indicates the person is an adult, ORR will coordinate with DHS for appropriate actions, potentially including transfer out of ORR custody.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions and usage of emergency or influx facilities (85% capacity rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR defines 'influx' as when net bed capacity in standard programs is 85 percent or greater for seven consecutive days; 'emergency' includes events preventing timely placement or transport. Emergency or influx facilities may be used temporarily to house children when standard capacity is strained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This departs from FSA's numeric approach; 85 percent threshold aligns with ORR experience. Emergency/influx facilities may be unlicensed or exempted from licensing but must meet ORR standards and comply to greatest extent possible with state child welfare laws; placements at such facilities cease when capacity drops below threshold for seven days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contingency planning and regular reevaluation during emergency/influx
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR will codify guidelines for contingency planning and procedures during emergencies or influx, including regular reevaluation of the number of placements needed and adjustments to shelters, heightened supervision facilities, and transitional home beds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In event of emergency/influx preventing prompt placement in standard programs, ORR shall make all reasonable efforts to place each child in a standard program as expeditiously as possible; emergency facilities are temporary responses when speed is critical.
